resources.string: Visualise and measure the noise level around you as you navigate your surroundings!
For your measurements to be accurate, it is important that you calibrate your microphone.
In order to measure the sound level and place it on a map the application need to have access to sensitive sensors. Please tap on "Request" buttons.
To be able to match recorded audio levels with map coordinates, we need access to your live location during the time you’re making a measurement.
Listening to incoming audio requires you to grant permission for NoiseCapture to use your device’s microphone.

NoiseCapture is a free, **open-source** app for anyone curious about the sounds in their surroundings. By recording and sharing your local sound environment, you help build a living, **open noise map**, helping communities, researchers, and policymakers understand and improve our acoustic landscapes.
Join a growing community of citizen scientists. Whether you’re in a bustling city or a quiet village, your data helps build a clearer picture of our sonic world.

- **Record and analyse:** Capture the sounds around you with your smartphone. Just hit record and let the app do the rest. - **Contribute to the community:** Your recordings join others to show how sound shapes our cities, parks, and streets. - **Privacy and transparency come first**: Sharing your measurements is always optional. All the data you decide to send is **completely anonymised**, then made available to everyone in open-access.
How familiar are you with acoustics?
This helps us contextualise measurements (e.g., flagging unusual readings for beginners), and offer helpful tips along the way if needed. You can change this anytime in **Settings**.

To measure the sounds around you, NoiseCapture needs access to your microphone. **Don’t worry, we never store or send your actual recordings.** Only anonymous acoustic indicators (like volume levels) are processed. For more details, check out our [privacy policy](https://noise-planet.org/NoiseCapture_privacy_policy.html).

In order to match analysed acoustic indicators to GPS coordinates to create community noise level maps, we need to access your location. All collected data is completely anonymous and we don’t collect any location data outside of measurements. See our privacy policy for more details.

The NoiseCapture app is currently recording surrounding audio to analyse acoustic parameters. Don't kill the app if you want the recording session to keep going.

Both microphones will measure the average surrounding noise level over a given period of time. The NoiseCapture app will apply a compensation gain to your microphone so that future measurements should match the reference output.
This microphone is not yet calibrated
Microphone should be placed at least two meters away from the sound source.
If calibration is done indoors, avoid being in one of the room corners.
Microphone should not be facing the sound source.
Avoid making noises close to the microphones.
Put the phone on a table instead of holding it in your hand.
Try using one of the following sound sources: pink noise, environmental noise (like cars passing in a street), or as fallback, people talking in the distance.

Use one of the following reference devices, in order of preference: a sound level meter, a smartphone with a calibrated external microphone, a smartphone with a calibrated internal microphone, small moving objects which sound levels are known to you.

The gain difference between your device and the reference is suspiciously high. We advise that you try calibrating again, following the tips. If you’re confident with your calibration method, you can still apply this suggested gain.
